Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

recognize verb

know again

also recognise, know again, I didn’t recognize you, identify, identification

classical

Quint. 11.2.17: nōn ipsa agnōscimus tantum
Cic. Fin. 5.42: eōs agnōscunt, ā quibus ēducantur

agnōscō, agnōscere, agnōvī, agnitum

verb, third conjugation

recognize, know again

Lewis & Short: agnōscere is to recognize what one has known before, cognōscere to get to know (see learn, find out). What one knows it by goes with ex: ex frūctū arbor agnōscitur (Vulg. Mt. 12.33, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • recognōscō, recognōscere, recognōvī, recognitum — know again, recall; more often, go over, review

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.57 (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ep. 83.2: diem meum recognōscam

    Lewis & Short: “to know again, recollect”, especially in Cicero; from the Augustan age on mostly “to look over, review”.

  • identificō, identificāre — identify

    verb, first conjugation · also used · modern · Traupman 331

    A modern word; classically agnōscere.

  • identificātiō, identificātiōnis f. — identification

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · Traupman 331

Examples

  • nam cum in loca aliqua post tempus reversī sumus, nōn ipsa agnōscimus tantum, sed etiam, quae in hīs fēcerīmus, reminīscimur

    for when we go back to a place after some time, we not only recognise it but also remember what we did thereQuint. 11.2.17

  • excipiunt plausū pavidōs gaudentque tuentēs Dardanidae, veterumque agnōscunt ōra parentum

    the Trojans greet the nervous boys with applause and delight in watching them, and recognise in them the faces of their forebearsVerg. A. 5.575–576

See also know, remember, recognize, notice.

SourcesLewis & Short: agnosco · Lewis & Short: recognosco
